situation:
You are the human resources manager at PARCELRISE FULFILMENT, a two-year-old company that stores, packs and ships orders for small online sellers. The chief operating officer (judge) has asked you to meet this afternoon about a training requirement that takes effect in nine weeks.

PARCELRISE sells a service, not a product; every carton on its shelves belongs to the seller who hired the company. Those sellers choose a fulfilment partner largely on dispatch reliability, and PARCELRISE won its accounts by promising that an order placed before two o'clock leaves the building the same day. The company is now spending the last of its first round of funding.

A new state regulation requires every worker who packs aerosols or batteries to finish a certified handling course before the deadline. Two agreements pull against each other. The contract with NORTHVIEW SUPPLY CO., the largest seller on the floor, guarantees same-day dispatch and charges a penalty for every day that slips. The staffing agreement with CROSSHAUL LABOR PARTNERS allows backfill on the packing line, but agency hours booked against a training block are billed at a premium rate.

Closing the packing floor for two days would certify the whole crew at once, but it would miss the same-day dispatch the NORTHVIEW contract guarantees and trigger the penalty. Running the course in small groups over ten weeks would protect dispatch, but the premium backfill hours would consume most of the funding the company has left, and the last group would not be certified until after the deadline.

The chief operating officer (judge) wants your recommendation on how PARCELRISE will meet the training requirement, how the packing line will run while the course is under way, what it does to the overhead the company carries whether or not orders arrive, and how that spending should be recorded in the books. You will present to the chief operating officer (judge), who will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the chief operating officer (judge) of PARCELRISE FULFILMENT. Business background is the same as the situation above. The new handling course has to be finished before the deadline, the NORTHVIEW SUPPLY CO. contract guarantees same-day dispatch, and the CROSSHAUL LABOR PARTNERS backfill hours are billed at a premium the company can barely absorb on what is left of its first round of funding.

You have asked the human resources manager to recommend how PARCELRISE will get its packers certified, how the packing line will run while that happens, what the decision does to the company's operating costs, and how the spending should be recorded in the books.

After the participant has presented, ask these questions:
judgeQuestions: Which course of action did you decide against, and what would it have cost us to take it?
If we had closed the packing floor instead, what would we have had to tell NORTHVIEW?
